strategist.thesis: Teradyne (TER) screens at opportunity 67.0 with an expectations gap of 19.0. Reality 78.0 reflects +57.9% TTM revenue growth, +30.2% operating margin and +41.8% ROIC; pricing 59.0 reflects a fair multiple and neutral price momentum. Primary theme exposure: Semiconductor Capacity Build (trend 66.0). Macro fit for Technology in a Goldilocks regime is 53.0/100.

AI Infrastructure: evidence that 'GPU supply, power availability, cooling, network bandwidth' is easing via Accelerators, optical/electrical interconnect, HBM memory, liquid cooling, on-site power

llm.thesis: Teradyne is a genuine fundamental acceleration story — TTM revenue +57.9% versus +30.3% the prior quarter, operating margin up 1,194bps to 30.2%, ROIC 41.8% with incremental ROIC of 122% — funded by a fortress balance sheet (zero debt, $350M net cash) while shrinking the share count 2.7%. The engine's +19pt expectations gap (reality 78 vs pricing 59) is real, but it is an acceleration gap, not a valuation gap: at 13.6x EV/Sales versus a 5-year median of 6.4x and 53x earnings (70th–80th percentile of its own history), the market has already paid for a multi-year semicap/HBM test upcycle. The genuine edge is narrower than the headline score: it rests on whether ATE operating leverage is structurally higher this cycle (advanced packaging and HBM test intensity per wafer) rather than merely cyclically peaking. The stock is 19.6% off its 52-week high after a +188% 12-month run and is consolidating above a rising 200-day — a healthy setup if bookings confirm, a classic distribution top if they do not. I would frame this as a momentum-with-earnings-confirmation position sized for high downside beta, not a value idea.
llm.fundamental_read: Growth is accelerating (revenue +57.9% vs +30.3% prior) with extreme operating leverage: incremental ROIC of 122% and a 1,194bps YoY operating margin expansion to 30.2% mean nearly all incremental revenue is dropping to profit on a largely fixed R&D/engineering cost base ($560M R&D, 12.5% of revenue). Quality is high — ROE 33%, ROA 23%, interest coverage 119x, net debt/EBITDA -0.24x, SBC just 1.7% of revenue — but cash conversion is the soft spot: FCF of $800M is only 70% of $1.15B net income, implying a working-capital build typical of an upcycle, and the 13.5% tax rate flatters the 153% EPS growth. Capital return is modest in yield terms ($501M buybacks, $78M dividends = 0.95% shareholder yield) because the equity is expensive, not because the company is stingy. The same operating leverage that produced +1,194bps on the way up is exactly what de-rates violently on a bookings air pocket in a test business with no debt cushion needed but no revenue cushion either.
llm.technical_read: Trend is intact and constructive: close 389.14 sits above the 20-day (360.77), 50-day (366.56) and 200-day (327.78) with a 50>200 uptrend, MACD histogram positive at +4.9, and RSI at 55.9 — momentum rebuilding, not overbought. But the tape is digesting: -8.9% over three months and -19.6% from the 52-week high after +188% over twelve, so the stock is 18.7% extended above its 200-day. Key levels: 360–367 as the first shelf (converged 20/50-day), with the 200-day near 328 roughly 16% lower — a close below that with negative relative strength is the stated thesis-break line.
llm.market_expectation: At 13.6x EV/Sales (80th percentile of its own 5-year range, vs a 6.4x median), 40.8x EV/EBITDA and a 1.3% FCF yield, the market is pricing Teradyne as a structural AI-test compounder rather than a cyclical ATE vendor — i.e. it expects the current ~30% operating margin and high-40s/50s growth to persist long enough to grow into the multiple. The PEG of 0.35 only looks cheap because it capitalizes a peak-cycle growth rate; consensus is implicitly assuming this is an early-innings capacity build (HBM/advanced-packaging test intensity), not a 2021-style digestion setup. The -19.6% drawdown from the high suggests some investors are already starting to price cycle risk, while Technology rotation at +73 keeps flows supportive.
what_market_misses: Mix and durability, not level: if the margin expansion is driven by test-intensity per device (HBM stacks, chiplets, higher parametric content) rather than unit volume, the 30% operating margin is a new floor rather than a cyclical peak — that would justify the premium multiple and is under-modeled by history-anchored mean-reversion screens (ai_inference).

The engine's own pricing score (59) is not cheap — the +19pt 'expectations gap' is driven by the acceleration component scoring 96, which is a second-derivative signal. Second-derivative signals mean-revert faster than multiples do; the gap can close by fundamentals decelerating rather than by price rising.

Cash conversion at 70% of net income is a quieter tell than the headline: in ATE upcycles receivables and inventory front-run revenue. If FCF conversion normalizes above 85% next quarter, it confirms the demand is shipping, not just being built.
The 13.5% tax rate is doing real work in the 153% EPS growth figure; any normalization compresses reported EPS growth without any change in operating performance.

Regime probabilities are essentially uniform (Goldilocks 26.3, Reflation 25.1, Contraction 24.9, Stagflation 23.7) — the 'Goldilocks' label carries almost no informational edge here, so macro is neither tailwind nor hedge for this position.

Two of the highest-signal inputs — estimate revisions and management guidance — are not connected (coverage 0.75). For a bookings-driven capital equipment name, guidance is the single most important variable, so the score is built on trailing data only.
catalysts: Next quarterly report (~90 days after the 2026-07-31 filing): the key line is book-to-bill / order commentary and whether FCF conversion recovers above 85%, not the EPS print.
Confirmation that test intensity per device is rising with HBM stack counts and advanced packaging — would re-rate TER from cyclical ATE to structural AI toll-taker.
Continued Technology sector rotation (+73, the only sector above +10 in the entire table) keeping passive and momentum flows directed into semicap.
Any inflection in the Robotics & Physical AI exposure (weighted 0.24) turning from drag to contributor would add an un-modeled growth leg.
Buyback acceleration on weakness — with zero debt and net cash, management has the capacity to lean into a drawdown.
risks: Valuation is the dominant risk: 13.6x EV/Sales at the 80th percentile versus a 6.4x 5-year median means ~2x of the last year's return is multiple expansion; a reversion toward history halves the stock even with flat revenue.
Extreme operating leverage is symmetric — incremental ROIC of 122% on the way up implies brutal decremental margins on a semis digestion phase.
Customer and end-market concentration in AI/HBM test; a single large customer's capex pause or a shift in HBM qualification timing can produce an abrupt bookings gap.
Export controls, China exposure and tariff regimes are perennial for semicap equipment and are not captured anywhere in the evidence set.
Theme exposure check already failed — exposure-weighted theme trend at 60.0 with Semiconductor Capacity Build at 66 is decelerating relative to price action.
Missing estimate-revision and guidance feeds mean the model is blind to the first place a semicap cycle turn shows up.
1.3% FCF yield gives essentially no valuation support in a drawdown; the buyer is paying for growth only.
thesis_break_conditions: TTM revenue growth falls below 41% (from 57.9%) — signals the acceleration has rolled over.
Operating margin compresses more than 200bps YoY from 30.2%, indicating the leverage was cyclical not structural.
FCF conversion deteriorates below ~60% for two consecutive quarters (currently 70%) — working capital absorbing rather than releasing cash.
Price closes more than 10% below the 200-day (i.e. below ~295) with negative relative strength.
Technology sector rotation score turns below -20 for two consecutive runs (currently +73).
Semiconductor Capacity Build theme trend drops below 45 (currently 66).
Combined Stagflation + Contraction regime probability exceeds 55% (currently 48.6%).
EV/Sales exceeds ~16x without a corresponding upward revision to forward growth — pure multiple expansion into a cyclical peak.
second_order_beneficiaries: Probe card and test interface suppliers (e.g. FormFactor): every incremental Teradyne tester needs consumable probe cards and load boards, and HBM/advanced-package test drives higher probe count per insertion — a razor-blade attached to TER's razor (ai_inference).

Test handler, thermal-control and burn-in board vendors: testing high-power AI silicon at socket requires active thermal management, which is a growing bill-of-materials line inside the test cell (ai_inference).
OSATs and advanced-packaging houses (ASE, Amkor) that must buy test capacity to serve HBM/chiplet volumes — TER's order book is their capex (ai_inference).

Contract manufacturers and precision subsystem suppliers who build the testers themselves; Teradyne's asset-light model ($265M capex on $4.46B revenue) means the physical build burden sits with suppliers (ai_inference).

Advantest as the direct ATE peer — if the driver is industry-wide test intensity rather than TER share gain, the peer captures the same structural demand, and relative valuation between the two is the cleaner expression (ai_inference).
EDA and design-for-test software vendors, since rising test cost per die pushes customers to optimize test time in silico before tape-out (speculative).
Power and cooling infrastructure for test floors — thousands of high-wattage insertions create the same electrical and thermal constraints as datacenters, at smaller scale (speculative).

epistemic_labels.statement: TTM revenue grew 57.9% versus 30.3% in the prior quarter, a 27.5pt acceleration.
Operating margin is 30.2%, up 1,194bps YoY; ROIC 41.8% with incremental ROIC of 122%.
Balance sheet carries zero debt and $350M net cash; net debt/EBITDA -0.24x; diluted shares down 2.7% YoY.
FCF of $800M represents 70% conversion of $1.15B net income; effective tax rate is 13.5%.
Valuation is 13.6x EV/Sales (80th percentile of 5y range vs 6.4x median), 52.9x P/E, 40.8x EV/EBITDA, 1.3% FCF yield.
Stock is +188% over 12 months, -19.6% from its 52-week high, -8.9% over 3 months, and 18.7% above its 200-day average.
Technology is the only sector with a rotation score above +10 (+73); all others range from +8 to -92.
The market expects the current growth and margin trajectory to persist long enough for the company to grow into a premium multiple.
A PEG of 0.35 is flattered by capitalizing a peak-cycle growth rate and should not be read as evidence of cheapness.
The 70% FCF conversion reflects a working-capital build typical of a semicap upcycle rather than earnings quality deterioration.
The +19pt expectations gap is driven by the acceleration component (96), a second-derivative signal that mean-reverts faster than valuation multiples.
Roughly uniform regime probabilities (26/25/25/24) mean the 'Goldilocks' label carries negligible directional information for this position.
Margin expansion is driven by rising test intensity per device (HBM stack counts, chiplets), making ~30% operating margin a structural floor rather than a cyclical peak.
The Robotics & Physical AI exposure could inflect from drag to growth contributor and is not reflected in current pricing.
Probe card, thermal-control and test-interface suppliers capture consumable economics that scale faster than tester unit sales.
